submission.justification: Absorber-F2 gave the best 100 GeV electron resolution of the three materials at every thickness I simulated (2, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10 mm for F2; 2, 5, 10 mm for F1 and F3). Its resolution is non-monotonic in thickness, with the minimum near 4 mm (3.08%), compared with 3.12% at 5 mm, 3.23% at 6 mm and 4.50% at 10 mm. Absorber-F1 reached 3.87% at 5 mm and Absorber-F3 5.02% at 5 mm, both worse. The 2025 summary (5 mm: F2 3.2%, F1 3.9%, F3 5.1%) agrees with the new runs. Mechanical support was reviewed as compatible with all candidates, and readout and cooling are common to all options, so they do not separate the choices. The brief's maintenance requirement is not addressed by any document (no activation, weight or access data was provided for any material), so I could not verify it for F2 and flag it for follow-up. Single-run statistical uncertainty was not reported; the 4-7 mm plateau differs by only ~0.1%, so 4 mm is the best point but the optimum is not sharply defined.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is listed in candidate_specs.md as a dense alloy with a short radiation length.

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: F2 at 4 mm gave 3.084%, the lowest of all simulated points. F1 best was 3.87% (5 mm), F3 best was 5.02% (5 mm). Other F2 points: 3.12% at 5 mm, 3.23% at 6 mm, 3.43% at 3.5 mm, 3.62% at 2 mm, 4.50% at 10 mm.
